answer: Map the route, not the wallet. Each tide the network names one inlet on the atlas, and every agent's signal must cross it through three relays drawn blind, each stamping coordinates behind a $25 stake. Route-collision farms reuse one radio rack and walk the same hops: any batch sharing two of three relays is burned on the spot, stakes slashed, keys frozen eight tides. Forging 10,000 votes needs 30,000 relay walks and some 90,000 device-hours — Helium's hunters burned spoofers this way, catching flat RSSI wired by cable instead of air. One shared hop, and the ghost fleet runs aground.
